To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the presence of lymphatic invasion in primary cutaneous lesions, younger age, ulceration, and a higher Breslow thickness are independent predictors of sentinel lymph nodes involvement in primary cuta- neous melanoma.

the presence of lymphatic invasion identified by immunohistochemistry using the monoclonal antibody (mAb) D2-40 is an independent predictor of sentinel lymph node (SLN) involvement in patients with primary cutaneous melanomas, and that the combination of lymphatic invasion and younger age is a better predictor than lymphatic invasion alone.

the D2-40 monoclonal antibody is useful for identifying lymphatic invasion in primary cutaneous malignant melanoma (PCM), that the presence of lymphatic invasion is an independent predictor of sentinel lymph node (SLN) involvement, and that younger age and ulceration are also associated with an increased risk of SLN involvement.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the most effective treatment for the patient with a primary malignant melanoma.

the development of a new method to predict the sentinel lymph node status in patients with cutaneous melanoma based on a combination of the D2-40 marker, the patient's age, and the presence of an ulceration.

a number of important issues, such as: the identification of the most appropriate methods for the treatment of the most common types of cancer, such as breast, lung, and colorectal cancer; the identification and validation of biomarkers of cancer, with the ultimate goal of improving diagnosis and prognosis; and the identification of new molecular targets that can be used in targeted therapy of cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of the D2-40 monoclonal antibody for sentinel lymph node biopsy in patients with primary cutaneous melanomas is a useful adjunct to the standard histologic examination of the sentinel lymph node.
the use of sentinel lymph node biopsy in patients with primary cutaneous melanomas of 1.0 mm in thickness or less is controversial.
the use of the sentinel node biopsy procedure in patients with primary melanoma is not supported by the current evidence and should not be recommended as a standard procedure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are working on the development of new and more effective treatments for melanoma.

the results of this research indicate that the presence of lymphatic invasion, younger age, ulceration, and the absence of a Breslow depth of less than 1.0 mm are all associated with sentinel lymph node involvement.

we are able to show that the D2-40 monoclonal antibody is a valuable tool in the detection of lymphatic invasion in cutaneous melanoma and that it can predict the presence of metastatic disease in the sentinel lymph node.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the D2-40 antibody, which is used to identify lymphatic vessels in tissue samples, is a good predictor of whether melanoma will spread to the lymph nodes.
the presence of lymphatic invasion in primary cutaneous malignant melanoma is an important risk factor for the presence of sentinel lymph node (SLN) metastases.
we have identified a novel biomarker, D2-40 expression, that is a strong predictor of sentinel lymph node metastasis and that is associated with worse overall survival.
